title: Adding and scaling points
description: Questions on scaling and adding points, lengths, moves as formulas and combining moves.

questions.question: What is $$3A$$ when $$A = (2, -1)$$?
questions.explanation: Multiplying a point by $$3$$ multiplies both coordinates by $$3$$ (:ref{#scalar-multiple}), so $$3A = (6, -3)$$. Multiplying only the first coordinate gives $$(6, -1)$$, and adding $$3$$ gives $$(5, 2)$$.

questions.question: For a number $$c > 1$$, what does $$P \mapsto cP$$ do to the plane?
options: It zooms out from the origin, moving every point $$c$$ times as far from $$O$$
It turns the plane about the origin
It moves every point $$c$$ units further from the origin
questions.explanation: For a positive $$c$$, multiplying by $$c$$ is the zoom by $$c$$ about the origin (:ref{#coordinates/origin-zoom}). Distances from $$O$$ are multiplied by $$c$$, not increased by $$c$$, so a point that starts far away moves further than one close in.

questions.question: What is $$0A$$, for any point $$A$$?
questions.explanation: Both coordinates get multiplied by $$0$$, so $$0A = (0, 0) = O$$ (:ref{#scalar-multiple}). Scaling by $$0$$ squashes the whole plane onto the origin.

questions.question: What does the map $$P \mapsto -P$$ do?
options: It flips the plane in the $$x$$-axis
It flips the plane in the $$y$$-axis
It turns the plane half a turn about the origin
It moves every point to the origin
questions.explanation: $$-P$$ is on the far side of $$O$$ from $$P$$, at the same distance, so $$O$$ is the midpoint of $$P$$ and $$-P$$. That makes $$P \mapsto -P$$ the reflection through $$O$$, which is the half turn about $$O$$ (:ref{#negative-half-turn}). Each flip in an axis changes only one sign.

questions.question: What does $$P \mapsto -2P$$ do?
options: Zooms by $$2$$ about the origin and then half turns about it
Moves every point $$2$$ units towards the origin
questions.explanation: For $$c < 0$$, $$cP = |c|(-P)$$, so multiplying by $$-2$$ is the zoom by $$2$$ together with the half turn about $$O$$, in either order (:ref{#negative-multiple}).

questions.question: Two points are $$5$$ apart. How far apart are their multiples by $$-3$$?
questions.explanation: Scaling by $$c$$ multiplies every distance by $$|c|$$ (:ref{#scale-distance}), so the answer is $$3 \times 5 = 15$$. A distance is never negative, so $$-15$$ can't be right.

questions.question: What is $$-\frac{1}{2}(4A)$$ the same as?
questions.explanation: Scaling twice multiplies the numbers: $$b(cA) = (bc)A$$ (:ref{#scale-twice}). Here $$-\frac{1}{2} \times 4 = -2$$.

questions.question: If $$bA = cA$$, which of these must be true?
questions.explanation: If $$A \ne O$$, then $$b = c$$ (:ref{#scale-cancel}). But if $$A = O$$, every multiple of $$A$$ is $$O$$, so $$bA = cA$$ holds for any $$b$$ and $$c$$. That's why the answer has to allow $$A = O$$.

questions.question: What is $$\frac{1}{2}(4, -6)$$?
questions.explanation: Halve both coordinates (:ref{#scalar-multiple}): $$(2, -3)$$. It is the point halfway from $$O$$ to $$(4, -6)$$.

questions.question: What is $$(2, 5) + (-3, 1)$$?
questions.explanation: Add the first coordinates and the second coordinates (:ref{#point-sum}): $$(2 - 3, 5 + 1) = (-1, 6)$$.

questions.question: Reading points as steps from the origin, what does $$A + B$$ mean?
options: Go to $$A$$ and then come back by $$B$$
The longer of the two steps
Take the step $$A$$, then the step $$B$$ from where you end up
questions.explanation: Adding is one step after another: from the origin go to $$A$$, then take the step $$B$$ from there. Since $$A + B = B + A$$ (:ref{#sum-rules}), taking $$B$$ first lands in the same place.

questions.question: What step takes you from $$B = (3, 5)$$ to $$A = (7, 2)$$?
questions.explanation: The step from $$B$$ to $$A$$ is $$A - B$$ (:ref{#difference-step}): $$(7 - 3, 2 - 5) = (4, -3)$$. The answer $$(-4, 3)$$ is $$B - A$$, the step back the other way.

questions.question: How are $$A - B$$ and $$B - A$$ related?
options: $$B - A = -(A - B)$$, the same step reversed
They have nothing to do with each other
questions.explanation: $$A - B$$ takes you from $$B$$ to $$A$$, and $$B - A$$ from $$A$$ back to $$B$$. Each coordinate changes sign, so $$B - A = -(A - B)$$ (:ref{#point-difference}). They have the same length.

questions.question: Which point $$X$$ satisfies $$X + (1, 4) = (3, 1)$$?
questions.explanation: The only such point is $$(3, 1) - (1, 4) = (2, -3)$$ (:ref{#difference-step}). Check: $$(2, -3) + (1, 4) = (3, 1)$$.

questions.question: Which rule do points NOT obey, unlike numbers?
options: None of these: points obey all three
questions.explanation: Adding points works coordinate by coordinate, so each rule follows from the same rule for numbers (:ref{#sum-rules}). All three hold.

questions.question: What is $$3(A + B) - 2A$$?
questions.explanation: $$3(A + B) = 3A + 3B$$ (:ref{#scale-sum-rules}), and $$3A - 2A = A$$, so the answer is $$A + 3B$$. Scaling and adding rearrange like numbers.

questions.question: How is $$(-2, 5)$$ written with the unit points $$E_1$$ and $$E_2$$?
questions.explanation: Every point is $$a_1E_1 + a_2E_2$$ with its own coordinates (:ref{#unit-combination}): $$2$$ steps back along the $$x$$-axis and $$5$$ up.

questions.question: What is the midpoint of $$(-1, 4)$$ and $$(5, -2)$$?
questions.explanation: The midpoint is half the sum (:ref{#midpoint-formula}): $$\frac{1}{2}(4, 2) = (2, 1)$$. The answer $$(4, 2)$$ forgets to halve, and $$(3, -3)$$ is half the difference.

questions.question: To prove $$M = \frac{1}{2}(A + B)$$ is the midpoint of $$AB$$, what must be shown besides $$d(A, M) = d(M, B)$$?
options: That $$M$$ lies on the segment $$AB$$, which follows from $$d(A, M) + d(M, B) = d(A, B)$$
questions.explanation: Many points are the same distance from $$A$$ and $$B$$: the whole perpendicular bisector. The midpoint is the one on the segment, and rule 1 of :ref{#distance-and-angles/segment-rules} puts $$M$$ there because the two halves add up to $$d(A, B)$$ (:ref{#midpoint-formula}).

questions.question: The points $$O$$, $$A = (1, 6)$$, $$C$$, $$B = (4, 3)$$ go round a parallelogram in that order. What is $$C$$?
questions.explanation: The far corner of the parallelogram on $$A$$ and $$B$$ is $$A + B = (5, 9)$$ (:ref{#parallelogram-law}). Half of that is where the diagonals cross, not a corner.

questions.question: What does this chapter prove about the four points $$O$$, $$A$$, $$A + B$$, $$B$$?
options: Opposite sides are equal and parallel
Opposite sides are equal, and the diagonals have the same midpoint
The angles are all right angles
questions.explanation: Both facts in :ref{#parallelogram-law} come from lengths and midpoints. That the opposite sides are also parallel needs lines in coordinates, which come in the next chapter.

questions.question: What is the length $$|(-6, 8)|$$?
questions.explanation: $$|A| = \sqrt{a_1^2 + a_2^2}$$ (:ref{#norm}), so $$\sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10$$. The answer $$100$$ forgets the square root, and $$14$$ adds the sizes of the coordinates.

questions.question: If $$|A| = 5$$, what is $$|-3A|$$?
questions.explanation: $$|cA| = |c|\,|A|$$ (:ref{#norm-scale}), so $$|-3A| = 3 \times 5 = 15$$. A length is never negative.

questions.question: Which of these equals $$d(A, B)$$?
questions.explanation: The distance between two points is the length of the step between them: $$d(A, B) = |A - B| = |B - A|$$ (:ref{#distance-norm}). The lengths of $$A$$ and $$B$$ alone don't decide it.

questions.question: If $$|A| = 3$$ and $$|B| = 4$$, which value of $$|A + B|$$ is impossible?
questions.explanation: By :ref{#norm-triangle}, $$|A + B| \le 3 + 4 = 7$$, so $$8$$ is impossible. By :ref{#norm-difference} it is at least $$1$$. Every value from $$1$$ to $$7$$ happens for some angle between the steps; $$5$$ is when they are at right angles.

questions.question: Two phones are $$9$$ km and $$4$$ km from the same mast. What can you say for sure about the distance between them?
options: It is at least $$5$$ km and at most $$13$$ km
questions.explanation: Put the mast at $$O$$ and the phones at $$A$$ and $$B$$. Then $$|A - B| \le 9 + 4$$ by :ref{#norm-triangle}, and $$|A - B| \ge 9 - 4$$ by :ref{#norm-difference}. Which value in between depends on where the phones are.

questions.question: Which is the unit point in the direction of $$(-7, 24)$$?
questions.explanation: $$|(-7, 24)| = \sqrt{49 + 576} = 25$$, and dividing by the length gives the unit point (:ref{#direction}). Dividing by $$17 = 24 - 7$$ doesn't give length $$1$$, and the last option points the opposite way.

questions.question: Which of these is a unit point?
questions.explanation: A unit point has length $$1$$ (:ref{#unit-point}). $$\frac{9}{25} + \frac{16}{25} = 1$$, so $$\left(\frac{3}{5}, -\frac{4}{5}\right)$$ is one. $$(1, 1)$$ has length $$\sqrt{2}$$ and $$\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$$ has length $$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$.

questions.question: Why does $$O$$ have no direction?
options: Because $$\frac{1}{|O|}O$$ would divide by $$0$$, and no unit point is a positive multiple of $$O$$
questions.explanation: Every multiple of $$O$$ is $$O$$, which has length $$0$$, so no multiple of it is a unit point. That's why :ref{#direction} needs $$A \ne O$$.

questions.question: Which set is the circle with centre $$A$$ and radius $$r$$?
questions.explanation: $$X$$ is on the circle when $$d(A, X) = r$$, which is $$|X - A| = r$$ (:ref{#circle-slide}). $$|X + A| = r$$ is the circle with centre $$-A$$, and $$|X| = r$$ has centre $$O$$.

questions.question: Under $$P \mapsto -2P$$, where does the circle with centre $$O$$ and radius $$3$$ go?
options: To the circle with centre $$O$$ and radius $$-6$$
To the circle with centre $$(-2, -2)$$ and radius $$3$$
To the circle with centre $$O$$ and radius $$6$$
questions.explanation: Scaling by $$c \ne 0$$ sends this circle to the one with radius $$|c| \cdot 3 = 6$$ and the same centre (:ref{#circle-scale}). The half turn part spins the circle round, which leaves it where it was.

questions.question: Where does the slide $$T_{(4, 3)}$$ send $$(1, 6)$$?
Where does the half turn about $$Q = (2, -1)$$ send $$P = (5, 3)$$?
questions.explanation: $$H_Q(P) = 2Q - P$$ (:ref{#half-turn-formula}): $$(4, -2) - (5, 3) = (-1, -5)$$. Check: the midpoint of $$(5, 3)$$ and $$(-1, -5)$$ is $$(2, -1) = Q$$. The answer $$(-5, -3)$$ is the half turn about $$O$$ instead.

questions.question: Why is $$2Q - P$$ the half turn of $$P$$ about $$Q$$?
options: Because $$Q$$ is the midpoint of $$P$$ and $$2Q - P$$
Because it is twice as far from $$O$$ as $$Q$$
Because it has the same length as $$P$$
questions.explanation: $$\frac{1}{2}(P + (2Q - P)) = Q$$, so $$Q$$ is the midpoint by :ref{#midpoint-formula}. A point and its reflection through $$Q$$ are exactly the pairs with midpoint $$Q$$ (:ref{#isometries/point-reflection}).

questions.question: Where does the zoom by $$3$$ about $$Q = (1, 2)$$ send $$P = (2, 4)$$?
questions.explanation: $$Z_{r,Q}(P) = Q + r(P - Q)$$ (:ref{#zoom-formula}). The step from $$Q$$ to $$P$$ is $$(1, 2)$$, three times that is $$(3, 6)$$, and $$(1, 2) + (3, 6) = (4, 8)$$. The answer $$(6, 12)$$ zooms about the origin instead.

questions.question: Where does the zoom by $$\frac{1}{2}$$ about $$(4, 0)$$ send $$(0, 6)$$?
questions.explanation: The step from $$(4, 0)$$ to $$(0, 6)$$ is $$(-4, 6)$$. Half of it is $$(-2, 3)$$, and taking that from $$(4, 0)$$ lands at $$(2, 3)$$ (:ref{#zoom-formula}), the midpoint of the two points.

questions.question: Which formula flips the plane in the $$x$$-axis?
questions.explanation: Points on the $$x$$-axis stay put and points above it go the same distance below, so only $$y$$ changes sign (:ref{#axis-reflections}). $$(-x, y)$$ flips in the $$y$$-axis, and $$(-x, -y)$$ is the half turn.

questions.question: Where does the flip in the line $$y = x$$ send $$(4, -3)$$?
questions.explanation: The flip in $$y = x$$ swaps the coordinates (:ref{#diagonal-reflection}), giving $$(-3, 4)$$.

questions.question: Where does the quarter turn $$G_{90}$$ about the origin send $$(4, -3)$$?
questions.explanation: $$G_{90}(x, y) = (-y, x)$$ (:ref{#quarter-turn}), so $$(4, -3) \mapsto (3, 4)$$. As a check, $$E_1 = (1, 0)$$ goes to $$E_2 = (0, 1)$$, which is anticlockwise.

questions.question: Which of these maps is NOT an isometry?
questions.explanation: $$P \mapsto 2P$$ doubles every distance (:ref{#scale-distance}). The others are a slide, a half turn about $$(1, 1)$$ and a flip, which all keep distances (:ref{#formula-isometries}).

questions.question: Which move has a whole line of fixed points?
options: The flip in the line $$y = x$$
questions.explanation: A flip leaves every point of its mirror where it is, so $$S$$ fixes the line $$y = x$$. A slide by $$A \ne O$$ fixes nothing, and a half turn or the quarter turn fixes only its centre (:ref{#formula-fixed-points}).

questions.question: Which points does $$P \mapsto 3P - (4, 2)$$ fix?
questions.explanation: Solve $$P = 3P - (4, 2)$$: then $$2P = (4, 2)$$ and $$P = (2, 1)$$. In fact the map is $$(2, 1) + 3(P - (2, 1))$$, the zoom by $$3$$ about $$(2, 1)$$, whose only fixed point is its centre (:ref{#formula-fixed-points}).

questions.question: What is the slide by $$(2, 1)$$ followed by the slide by $$(-5, 3)$$?
questions.explanation: Slides combine by adding their steps (:ref{#slide-compose}): $$(2, 1) + (-5, 3) = (-3, 4)$$. The order doesn't matter.

questions.question: What undoes the slide $$T_{(3, -2)}$$?
questions.explanation: $$T_A^{-1} = T_{-A}$$ (:ref{#slide-inverse}): slide back by the opposite step.

questions.question: What undoes the zoom $$Z_4$$ about the origin?
questions.explanation: Zooms about the origin combine by multiplying, so $$Z_{1/4} \circ Z_4 = Z_1$$, which moves nothing (:ref{#zoom-compose}).

questions.question: What is the half turn about $$Q = (1, 0)$$ followed by the half turn about $$M = (3, 2)$$?
questions.explanation: $$H_M \circ H_Q = T_{2(M - Q)}$$ (:ref{#two-half-turns}). Here $$M - Q = (2, 2)$$, so the slide is by $$(4, 4)$$, twice the step between the centres.

questions.question: What is the half turn about $$Q$$ done twice?
questions.explanation: Set $$M = Q$$ in :ref{#two-half-turns}: the slide by $$2(Q - Q) = O$$, which moves nothing. Two half turns make a full turn.

questions.question: Which recipe gives the zoom by $$r$$ about the point $$Q$$?
options: Zoom by $$r$$ about $$O$$, then slide by $$Q$$
Slide by $$Q$$, zoom by $$r$$ about $$O$$, then slide by $$-Q$$
Slide by $$-Q$$, zoom by $$r$$ about $$O$$, then slide by $$Q$$
questions.explanation: Move $$Q$$ to the origin, do the zoom there, and move back: $$Z_{r,Q} = T_Q \circ Z_r \circ T_{-Q}$$ (:ref{#zoom-composite}). The composite is read from right to left, so $$T_{-Q}$$ happens first.

questions.question: Zoom by $$\frac{1}{2}$$ about the origin, slide by $$A$$, then zoom by $$2$$ about the origin. What is the result?
questions.explanation: This is $$Z_2 \circ T_A \circ Z_2^{-1}$$, which is $$T_{2A}$$ (:ref{#conjugate-slide}). Seen on a map zoomed by $$2$$, a slide looks twice as long.

questions.question: What is the flip in the $$x$$-axis followed by the flip in the $$y$$-axis?
questions.explanation: $$(x, y) \mapsto (x, -y) \mapsto (-x, -y)$$, which is the half turn about $$O$$ (:ref{#combining-moves-flips}). Mirrors at a right angle make a half turn, as the Isometries chapter showed with pictures.

questions.question: $$S(x, y) = (y, x)$$ and $$R_1(x, y) = (x, -y)$$. Which statement is true?
options: Both composites are the half turn
questions.explanation: $$S(R_1(1, 3)) = S(1, -3) = (-3, 1) = G_{90}(1, 3)$$, but $$R_1(S(1, 3)) = R_1(3, 1) = (3, -1)$$, the clockwise quarter turn (:ref{#combining-moves-flips}). So the order of two flips matters.

questions.question: What is $$(1, 0, 2) + (3, -1, 4)$$?
questions.explanation: Add each of the three coordinates (:ref{#space-operations}).

questions.question: What is $$|(2, 3, 6)|$$?
questions.explanation: $$\sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7$$ (:ref{#space-norm}). The answer $$\sqrt{13}$$ forgets the third coordinate.

questions.question: What is the midpoint of $$(1, 0, 2)$$ and $$(3, -2, 4)$$?
questions.explanation: Half the sum (:ref{#space-midpoint}): $$\frac{1}{2}(4, -2, 6) = (2, -1, 3)$$.

questions.question: How far apart are $$(4, 1, -2)$$ and $$(1, 5, 10)$$?
questions.explanation: The step between them is $$(-3, 4, 12)$$, with length $$\sqrt{9 + 16 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13$$ (:ref{#space-norm-rules}). The answer $$5$$ uses only the first two coordinates.

questions.question: In space, what is true of the map $$A \mapsto -A$$?
options: It is a half turn about the $$z$$-axis
It keeps distances, but it is not a turn about any line
It fixes every point of a line
questions.explanation: It keeps distances, since $$|(-A) - (-B)| = |A - B|$$, but a turn about a line fixes that line, and $$A \mapsto -A$$ fixes only $$O$$ (:ref{#space-negative}). It swaps left and right hands, like a mirror. In the plane, the same formula is the half turn.
